identity.title: ALMA full polarization observations of PKS 1830-211 during its record-breaking flare of 2019

paper_type_evidence.quote: PKS 1830$-$211 was observed with ALMA in full polarization mode on 2019 April 11.

redshift_or_distance.value: absorber at z=0.89 (molecular absorber in front of the blazar)

evidence.quote: The source has two bright and compact images (hereafter labelled NE and SW), separated by 1$''$ and delayed in time by $\sim$26 days

question.value: How do the polarization properties of the lensed blazar PKS 1830-211 differ between its two lensed images and vary on intra-hour timescales during its 2019 gamma-ray flare, and can differential polarimetry be validated with full-polarization data?

evidence.quote: Here we report full polarization radio-millimeter observations of PKS 1830$-$211 obtained with ALMA close in time to this exceptional peak of the $\gamma$-ray activity.
The full-polarization calibration allows us to validate the technique of differential polarimetry.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00692.S.
The Band 6 receivers were used

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four 1.875 GHz spectral windows at ~234, 236, 247, 249 GHz, 1.95 MHz channels

evidence.quote: the correlator was configured to cover four independent 1.875 GHz wide spectral windows, centered at $\sim 234$, 236, 247, and 249 GHz, with a spectral resolution of 1.95 MHz per channel.
The resulting beam is $0.47 ''\times 0.31''$, with a position angle $-83^\circ$.

observing_dates.value: 2019 April 11, two consecutive executions over ~2 h

evidence.quote: Observations were done in two consecutive executions over a time span of about two hours.

provided.value: gamma-ray light curve of the flare

evidence.quote: see Fig. [3](#fig:gamma-lc), generated from Fermi-LAT observations

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA, two-step: standard calibration then full-polarization calibration

evidence.quote: The data calibration was done within the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA[^1]) package, following a two-step procedure.

flux_calibrator.value: J2000-1748 as absolute flux calibrator; bootstrapped to J1832-2039

evidence.quote: The quasar J2000-1748 was also used as absolute flux calibrator.
We estimate a flux accuracy better than 10%, based on the ALMA monitoring data of this source.

self_calibration.value: phase-only, 6 s solint, all four spws combined, on Stokes I continuum

evidence.quote: applying phase-only gain corrections at each 6 s integration and combining all four spectral windows to a common solution.

task.value: tclean for Stokes I, Q, U separately; immath for m and EVPA

evidence.quote: The CASA task `tclean` was executed to reconstruct the images of PKS 1830$-$211 in Stokes I, Q, and U, separately.
Uniform visibility weighting was used in the image deconvolution.

masking.value: same mask for Q and U as for Stokes I

evidence.quote: The CLEANing of Stokes Q and U was executed using the same mask as in the CLEANing of Stokes I.
The resulting beam is $0.47 ''\times 0.31''$, with a position angle $-83^\circ$.

what.value: Full-polarization calibration follows standard ALMA procedure

evidence.quote: following the standard ALMA calibration procedure (cite: Nagai)
For a thorough discussion of the advantages of visibility model-fitting in this case, see (cite: mar14).
derived from Eq. 11 of (cite: mar16), which is the exact expression for differential polarimetry

unstated_but_needed: tclean cell size, image size, iteration/threshold and mask definition
line-free channel selection and flagged absorption/atmospheric ranges
uvmultifit source-model settings and error estimation
fit method for Faraday RM and the NE/SW flux ratio function

method.value: Standard calibration, flagging of absorption lines, polarization calibration with J1924-2914, phase-only self-cal on Stokes I

evidence.quote: The quasar J 1924$-$2914 was observed as the polarization calibrator.

key_parameters.value: self-cal solint 6 s, all spws combined

evidence.quote: applying phase-only gain corrections at each 6 s integration and combining all four spectral windows to a common solution.

validation.value: Dynamic range improved by factor 2-3 after self-cal, reaching >~1000

evidence.quote: the dynamic range (DR; i.e., the ratio of peak flux to rms noise level in the image) improved by a factor 2–3 after self-calibration

analysis_steps.goal: Image Stokes I,Q,U and derive m and EVPA

method.value: tclean per Stokes, immath pixel-wise m and phi

evidence.quote: The images of the degree of linear polarization, $m$, and EVPA, $\phi$, were computed pixel-wise from the Stokes Q and U images with the CASA task `immath`

method.value: Each ~410 s scan split in three segments; Stokes I, Q, U of both images fitted independently with uvmultifit; differential NE/SW approach

evidence.quote: Each ALMA scan (with a typical duration of 410 seconds) was divided into three segments of equal length and the Stokes parameters I, Q, and U of PKS 1830$-$211 were fitted independently to each scan subdivision.

assumptions.value: Both lensed images point-like within the beam

evidence.quote: Since both lensed images of the blazar are point-like within the ALMA beam

validation.value: Differential approach removes residual instrumental effects common to both images

evidence.quote: we search for relative changes between the NE and SW polarization states, in order to remove any possible residual instrumental effect

method.value: Fit XX and YY flux ratios in 15 segments per scan, compute Rpol=(rho_X/rho_Y-1)/2 vs source rotation, compare with prediction from full-pol Stokes parameters

evidence.quote: In these fits, we divided each scan into 15 segments of equal duration to perform an intra-observation analysis

key_parameters.value: feed rotation beta = 45 deg in Band 6

evidence.quote: which are rotated by $\beta = 45^\circ$ with respect to the horizontal coordinates in Band 6

validation.value: Good agreement; chi2 decreases 10-15% by rotating SW image 2-5 deg

evidence.quote: the fit improves slightly (a decrease of 10–15% in the $\chi^2$) by rotating the SW image by 2$-$5 degrees

analysis_steps.goal: Faraday rotation fit of differential EVPA

method.value: Thin Faraday screen (phi ∝ lambda^2) fit to NE-SW EVPA difference at each time bin

evidence.quote: we used a model of thin Faraday screen (i.e., $\phi \propto \lambda^2$ law) to fit the EVPA difference between the two images at each time bin.
The data calibration was done within the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA[^1]) package
The fitting was performed with the Python-based task `uvmultifit` (cite: mar14)
a fractional polarization peak of 14% (in the SW image, with a flux density of 2.34 Jy)
5.4% (in the NE image, with a flux density of 2.10 Jy)
its EVPA ($-24$ degrees) is rotated $\sim$15 degrees with respect to that of the SW
a clear linear increase in the EVPA difference between the two images (see Fig. [2](#fig:curves)A) at a rate of about two degrees per hour
we estimate a variation from $\Delta\alpha \sim -0.19$ to $\Delta\alpha \sim -0.05$ between the start and end of the observations

results_numeric.quantity: Weighted mean RM of differential NE-SW

evidence.quote: The weighted average of all the RM measurements is $(3.4 \pm 1.7)\times 10^4$ rad m$^{-2}$.
The maximum $R_{pol}$ measured in our 2019 observations ($\sim 0.1$; Fig. [4](#fig:diffpol))

findings_qualitative.value: Polarization intensity appears suppressed during the gamma-ray flare; consistent with stronger magnetic turbulence

evidence.quote: the polarization intensity of the blazar was somehow suppressed during the $\gamma$-ray flare

claims.hypothesis: Do the NE and SW images show different polarization reflecting intrinsic evolution?
claims.result: NE fractional polarization ~3 times lower than SW; EVPA offset ~15 deg
claims.finding: Intrinsic polarization evolved within the ~26 day delay; polarization suppressed during flare

evidence.quote: The leading NE image has a fractional polarization about three times lower than the SW image

claims.result: EVPA difference rising ~2 deg/h; relative fractional polarization changed ~10%
claims.finding: Significant variability on ~1 h timescales, consistent with magnetic turbulence

evidence.quote: The differential electric vector position angle varied at a rate of about 2 degrees per hour during the time span of $\sim 2$ h of our observations.

claims.hypothesis: Does full-pol calibration validate differential polarimetry?
claims.experiment: Compare Rpol from XX/YY fits to full-pol prediction

evidence.quote: There is good agreement between the dual-polarization measurements and the full-polarization prediction

limitations_admitted.value: Faraday rotation analysis is limited; RM only tentative and consistent with zero at 2 sigma

evidence.quote: All the fitted values are compatible with zero at a 2$\sigma$ level

referee_caveats_inferred: Turbulent-cell interpretation rests on a single epoch
Cannot tell which lensed image changes its spectral index
Time-delay comparison assumes negligible differential effects from microlensing or the lens
